points.description: States that the compiler replaces/expands the function call with the function's code (a copy of the function body is inserted at the point of the call). Equivalent wording such as 'substitutes the body', 'expands inline', 'pastes the code' earns the marks. A vague answer that only says the function is 'faster' or 'special' without stating code is copied/substituted earns nothing.

levels.says: Says the function code is copied/inserted but not clearly at the call location, or only says the call is replaced, without mention of code being copied

points.description: States that this happens at every place/each time the function is called (a separate copy for each call), rather than one shared copy being jumped to.

States that this is done at compile time instead of a normal function call (no call/jump and return, no call overhead/stack frame), OR notes the purpose of avoiding call overhead. Either one suffices.

rubric.notes: The model answer (copy of function code at every call site) must earn full 5/5: P1 and P2 are in it, and P3 is satisfied by the idea that the call is replaced by the code, so award P3 if the answer says the call is replaced by the copy rather than a normal call. Part marks for stating only that code is substituted without location. No marks for vague statements.
